title: What If You Tried to Outrun a Tsunami?

scenes.text: What if you tried to outrun a tsunami? The wave is slower than you think, until it isn't.
In the open ocean a tsunami travels over 500 miles an hour, as fast as a jet airliner.
Out there it is rarely more than three feet high, so ships passing over it often don't notice.
The wavelength can span hundreds of miles, so the whole ocean surface moves as one long swell.
Near shore it slows to roughly 20 to 30 miles an hour, but the wave grows taller as it slows.
That is faster than almost anyone can run for long. The real answer is height: go uphill, not away.

description:
What if you tried to outrun a tsunami?
It crosses oceans at over 500 mph, then slows to 20 to 30 mph near shore while growing taller.
What should we run through next?
